minutes.headline: Town meeting narrowly passed sweeping town-employee benefit/hiring changes over a select board member's objection.
minutes.summary: This was Lunenburg's fall 2024 special town meeting, covering fifteen warrant articles: budget transfers, an elderly tax exemption COLA, a rewritten water supply protection bylaw, several revolving funds, a request to explore selling or leasing the Brooks House, and two lengthy, contested articles amending the town's salary administration plan to add sick banks, holiday pay, merit awards and employment contracts aimed at staff recruitment and retention. The salary plan articles drew extended public debate over the lack of a seated Personnel Committee and process speed but passed; a Marshall Park renovation appropriation and a citizen petition article were both passed over without action.

what_happened.line: Voters passed sweeping changes to town-employee pay and benefits, despite objections over the empty Personnel Committee seat.
A rewrite of the water supply protection bylaw passed, after residents raised concerns about lake water withdrawal and which map applied.
Voters asked the select board to study selling or leasing the Brooks House, without authorizing any sale.
A Marshall Park renovation appropriation was passed over after cost estimates came in far higher than expected.
Voters approved additional funds for the FY25 school operating budget and for current-year salary and health insurance lines.

why_it_matters: The salary plan changes touch pay, sick time, holidays and hiring contracts for every town employee, and were adopted without a seated Personnel Committee to vet them.
The water bylaw rewrite governs protections around the town's water supply and the lakes near Hickory Hills, an area several residents spoke about directly.
Residents should expect a revised Marshall Park proposal at spring town meeting, and a select-board report on the Brooks House's future.
